title: Ordinary coefficient and module comparison for component projections
statement: Let T,V be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme], P=π₀(T), Q=π₀(V), with canonical component projections [def-zl-generic-component-data], and assume π_V inverse image is an equivalence. For every condensed ring Λ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], fix any ring-valued sheaves A,AU,AV with isomorphisms presenting Λ and its canonical coefficient rings on T and V [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Then there are ring inverse images LU,LV left adjoint to actual component restriction; comparisons LU(A/P)≅AU and LV(A/Q)≅AV; and γ:A/Q→F_V*AV equal to the adjunction unit followed by the second comparison. Their underlying set functors are precisely the component inverse images. The terminal component test object is isomorphic to V, and evaluation of γ along this isomorphism is a ring isomorphism eΓ. There is an additive equivalence E:Mod(A/Q)≌Mod(AV) left adjoint to module pushforward along γ. For every commutative discrete R there is an additive equivalence ER of the constant-R module-sheaf categories, preserving constant realization, such that any scalar-extension left adjoints along maps to A/Q and AV agreeing on global constant sections fit into FS⋙E≅ER⋙FV (constant-ring compatibility of [def-zl-generic-component-data]). These data are bundled by GenericComponentCoefficientData. This result concerns ordinary sheaves and ordinary modules only; it has no derived-category assumption.

proof.text: For an affine scheme Z, pullback of an absolute profinite test set E is the component test object for π₀(Z)×E→π₀(Z). They have the same product locally ringed space |Z|×E and inverse-image structure sheaf. The uniqueness in the canonical component construction makes this identification natural. Its adjunction mate identifies the structural profinite point inverse image with component inverse image after slicing.

proof.text: Use the given isomorphisms presenting the condensed ring and its two coefficient inverse images. Lift each component inverse image to ring sheaves by transporting addition, zero, negation, multiplication and one using its finite-product comparisons. Sheafification makes these the left adjoints to ring restriction. The structural identity of Step 1 identifies their values on A/P and A/Q with AU and AV, the two canonical coefficient rings. Set γ to the displayed unit composite.

proof.text: Finite-limit preservation sends the terminal profinite-over-Q object to the terminal pro-etale object V, yielding t. Since the set inverse image over V is an equivalence, transporting ring operations makes its ring adjunction an equivalence as well. Its unit is invertible, so γ and then terminal restriction along t give the normalized ring isomorphism eΓ.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.13, diagram (4.4) and the following coefficient paragraph

proof.text: Transport each module action μ:A×M→M and addition along that same finite-product equivalence and its ring comparison. The transported operations satisfy the module axioms because equivalences preserve their diagrams. Transport linear maps in the same way. The unit and counit commute with every operation and give inverse additive module equivalences. The direct module functor is actual restriction along F_V with the γ scalar action: the ordinary ring adjunction bijection restricts to linear maps precisely for that action. Hence the forward functor is left adjoint to SheafOfModules.pushforward γ.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.13, diagram (4.4) and the following coefficient paragraph

proof.text: Repeat module transport for the constant ring realizationRing J R to get ER. The two composites of constant realization are left adjoint to global sections and so canonically isomorphic. A map from the sheafified constant ring is determined by its composites with the constant-presheaf unit. Naturality along the unique arrows to the terminal object shows that equality on global constant sections implies equality of these composites at every object. Thus the normalized scalar maps give a commuting restriction-of-scalars square. Its left-adjoint square is FS⋙E≅ER⋙FV by uniqueness, as required. This also proves the empty-site and zero-ring cases without nonzero-section assumptions.

lean.statement:
theorem generic_component_coefficient_comparison
    (T V : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine T] [IsAffine V]
    [(genericComponentProjection V).inverse.IsEquivalence]
    (Λ : Profinite.CondensedRing.{u})
    (A : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) RingCat.{u + 1})
    (AU : Sheaf (topology T) RingCat.{u + 1})
    (AV : Sheaf (topology V) RingCat.{u + 1})
    (hA : Nonempty (Mon.mk ((sheafCompose (coherentTopology Profinite.{u})
      (forget₂ RingCat.{u + 1} Ab.{u + 1})).obj A) ≅ Λ))
    (hAU : Nonempty (Mon.mk ((sheafCompose (topology T)
      (forget₂ RingCat.{u + 1} Ab.{u + 1})).obj AU) ≅
        AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.coefficientRing T Λ))
    (hAV : Nonempty (Mon.mk ((sheafCompose (topology V)
      (forget₂ RingCat.{u + 1} Ab.{u + 1})).obj AV) ≅
        AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.coefficientRing V Λ)) :
    Nonempty (GenericComponentCoefficientData T V A AU AV)
